question: Can steepest descent under non-Euclidean matrix geometry and curvature-aware preconditioning be represented by one norm construction, and can that construction produce useful spectral-and-adaptive optimizers with provable reparameterization invariance?

key_findings.claim: Left/right and elementwise preconditioned matrix norms reduce their linear minimization oracles to an oracle in a transformed gradient space.
key_findings.evidence: Definitions 1-2 introduce the two norm families, while Theorem 1 maps the gradient into the preconditioned space, applies the base-norm oracle, and maps the direction back. Table 1 recovers normalized SGD, SignSGD, Muon, K-FAC, Shampoo, Adam, SOAP, and SPlus as instances.

key_findings.claim: The framework yields necessary and sufficient transformation rules for affine and coordinate-scale invariance of matrix-parameterized updates.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2 states that left/right preconditioners must transform with the two basis changes for affine invariance, while an elementwise preconditioner must scale elementwise with the parameter rescaling; Corollary 1 applies the latter condition to MuAdam-SANIA when epsilon is zero.

key_findings.claim: MuAdam combines Adam-style moment statistics with a spectral linear-minimization step by preconditioning both before and after Newton-Schulz orthogonalization.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 1 uses exponent p=1/4 for MuAdam and p=1/2 for MuAdam-SANIA, divides the bias-corrected momentum by the adaptive statistic, applies the Muon-style Newton-Schulz map, and divides a second time before updating parameters.

key_findings.claim: The empirical advantage is task-dependent rather than uniform.
key_findings.evidence: MuAdam leads the reported LoRA GLUE average, but AdamW leads full fine-tuning. On Qwen2-7B it beats both baselines on BoolQ and HellaSwag but trails on ARC-Challenge. On character Shakespeare it beats AdamW for three and four layers but not two layers.

method.core_idea: Encode curvature or coordinate adaptation inside a matrix norm, then derive the corresponding steepest-descent direction from the base norm's linear minimization oracle.
method.mechanism: Two-sided matrices represent Kronecker-style preconditioning and an elementwise matrix represents Adam-style scaling. The framework transforms the gradient, applies a selectable base geometry such as Frobenius, sign, or spectral, and transforms the direction back. MuAdam instantiates the spectral choice with adaptive moments and Newton-Schulz orthogonalization.
assumptions: The preconditioners are invertible or regularized enough for the inverse transformations.
The base-norm oracle has a unique solution in the invariance theorem.
Finite Newton-Schulz iterations adequately approximate the spectral oracle.
The epsilon-free invariance result remains a useful guide even though practical optimizers generally need numerical stabilization.

techniques.role: Makes geometry and curvature adaptation composable in one optimization abstraction.
Derives update directions by applying a base-norm oracle after preconditioning the gradient.
Places a Newton-Schulz spectral map between two adaptive scaling operations.
Characterizes exactly how preconditioners must change under basis or coordinate rescaling.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer MLP on original and exponentially rescaled Mushrooms features
evaluations.result: Adam-SANIA and MuAdam-SANIA retain overlapping original/scaled trajectories; MuAdam-SANIA matches or exceeds Adam-SANIA
evaluations.baseline: AdamW and Muon, whose trajectories degrade under rescaling

evaluations.setting: DistilBERT on eight GLUE tasks with LoRA and full fine-tuning
evaluations.result: Reported LoRA average is 0.7869 for AdaMuon/MuAdam-like method, versus 0.7663 AdamW and 0.7687 Muon; full AdamW is best at 0.8271

limitations: Reviewer-identified: the experiments are fine-tuning and small-language-model studies, not controlled pretraining-scale tests of optimizer efficiency or stability.
Reviewer-identified: best-over-learning-rate reporting and task-dependent wins do not establish a generally dominant optimizer.
Author-visible caveat: exact scale invariance for MuAdam-SANIA is proved only with epsilon equal to zero, whereas numerical implementations use epsilon.
Reviewer-identified: the unifying vocabulary does not itself prove that every combination of preconditioner and norm has favorable convergence or computational cost.
failure_modes: Near-singular adaptive statistics can make the transformed-space direction unstable.
An inaccurate or low-iteration polar-factor approximation can change the intended spectral geometry.
The double preconditioning can over-amplify low-variance coordinates.
Optimizer rankings may reverse across full fine-tuning, LoRA, model depth, or dataset.
reusable_insights: Treat optimizer design as the orthogonal choice of a geometry and a curvature estimator.
Check equivariance of state variables, not only the final update, when claiming reparameterization invariance.
Report per-task losses alongside aggregate scores because optimizer improvements are heterogeneous.
open_questions: Which preconditioner/base-norm combinations retain convergence guarantees under stochastic nonconvex training?
Does MuAdam preserve its advantage in compute-matched pretraining at billion-parameter scale?
Can epsilon-regularized variants obtain approximate invariance with a quantitative error bound?

competitive_landscape.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
competitive_landscape.difference: SOAP runs Adam-like adaptation in Shampoo's slowly changing eigenbasis; this paper abstracts that interaction as a preconditioned norm and instead proposes spectral MuAdam variants.

competitive_landscape.title: Shampoo: Preconditioned Stochastic Tensor Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: Shampoo supplies Kronecker-factored matrix statistics under Frobenius geometry; the reviewed framework makes the base geometry selectable and treats Shampoo as one instance.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimizing Neural Networks with Kronecker-factored Approximate Curvature
competitive_landscape.difference: K-FAC approximates natural-gradient curvature from activations and gradients; the reviewed work focuses on a norm-level representation of two-sided preconditioning and alternative linear-minimization geometries.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the strongest novelty is the algebraic packaging of two-sided and elementwise preconditioning with arbitrary matrix-norm oracles plus an explicit matrix-invariance criterion. The individual ingredients—Kronecker preconditioning, adaptive moments, spectral descent, and Newton-Schulz updates—substantially predate the paper, and the empirical evidence supports competitiveness rather than general superiority.
reviewer_notes: Read against the exact v3 extraction. Quantitative claims are confined to the paper's selected hyperparameter sweeps; the distinction between theorem-level exact invariance and stabilized implementation is reviewer emphasis. Competitor records were checked on arXiv on 2026-08-23.
